title: Nexa Commerce - integration ops scratchpad
content:
Call notes (2025-11-03) - Nexa Commerce onboarding call with Platform and Fulfillment teams

Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Nexa Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Nexa Platform), Tom Hsu (Nexa Ops), Alex Kim (Redwood Solutions)

High-level ask:
- Nexa wants LLM-based product classification + personalized description generation for their storefront and downstream catalog ingestion pipeline.
- Must run inference inside their VPC (data residency + PII) with bursty traffic around promotions (Black Friday pattern). Looking at Redwood Private (VPC) with option for Dedicated reserved pools for steady baseline.

Traffic profile & targets (customer-provided estimates):
- Baseline QPS: 10 qps steady for catalog enrichment jobs (batch), spikes up to 400 qps for live product description generation during campaigns for <2h windows.
- Typical prompt length: 120–250 tokens in + 60–120 tokens out.
- Latency SLO for storefront calls: p95 < 350ms. Offline enrichment jobs can be >2s.
- Cost sensitivity: target average model cost per call <= $0.03 (token-based economics).

Key technical constraints:
- All inference must not leave customer VPC; KMS-managed keys required for logs and model artifacts.
- Existing infra uses k8s (EKS) with GPU nodes already approved but low spare capacity — customer prefers Redwood-managed private control plane + customer compute for runtime to avoid heavy infra ops.
- Model choice: Nexa is open to Llama2-13B-Chat-8k quantized or Mistral 7B depending on quality/cost tradeoffs. They want side-by-side evals on their prompts.

Gotchas & implementation risks observed on call:
1) Burst handling: Their spike pattern (400 qps) needs pre-warming strategy and burst capacity. If we only do standard autoscaling, initial ramp will miss storefront p95 SLO. Suggestion: Dedicated reserved baseline + short-lived burst pool or cross-region fallback.
2) Token budget accounting: In-store description generation is called synchronously from user web requests; need strict per-request token caps and aggressive streaming to reduce tail latency.
3) KV cache cold start: For chat-style personalization (user history prefix), KV cache on quantized models can blow memory — need eviction policy by user session and approximate LRU shard sizing.
4) Logging & PII: They insist on user-provided KMS + audit logs stored in S3 behind VPC endpoint. Must ensure Redwood Console telemetry can be forwarded without plaintext copying to hosted plane.
5) Model drift: They plan to A/B multiple prompt templates and will need Redwood Optimize eval hooks to detect quality regressions tied to specific prompt sets.

Suggested Redwood config (initial proposal):
- Deployment: Redwood Private with control plane in Redwood, runtime in customer VPC (customer-managed nodes) — or full Private on-prem if needed.
- Baseline capacity: Dedicated pool = 16 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state QPS (estimate), with 8-GPU burst reserve for promotions (auto-provisioned through spot-like mechanism).
- Batching policy: latency-first with micro-batch (batch size <= 8, max wait 30ms) for storefront, throughput-first for enrichment jobs (batch up to 64, wait 250ms).
- Quantization: 4-bit quantized Llama2-13B candidate; evaluate Mistral7B for lower cost path. Provide bench harness with their 2000-sample prompt set.
- Caching: Prefix caching for catalog templates + per-SKU inference cache with 24h TTL for identical SKU text.
- Fallbacks: If customer runtime capacity exhausted, route non-sensitive enrichment to Redwood Hosted (requires opt-in) or degrade to shorter output length.

Unresolved questions (needs answers before design doc):
- Exact spike cadence (is 400 qps a per-minute peak or sustained 5-10 minute window?).
- Can Nexa accept a short cold-fallback to Hosted for non-PII data during extreme peaks?
- Do they want per-request cost telemetry surfaced in Redwood Console for product owners?
- What are their retention periods for console metrics and audit logs (30/90/365 days)?

Action items & owners
- Maya: run initial perf sim with 2000 prompt samples on Llama2-13B-4bit + Mistral7B. Deliver bench report w/ token cost estimate (due 2025-11-10).
- Ravi: confirm exact peak durations and provide 2-week request trace (due 2025-11-07).
- Sofia: validate KMS/HSM vendor and confirm networking (VPC endpoints, egress rules) (due 2025-11-12).
- Tom: share current k8s GPU node sizing and limitations (node types, spot usage) (due 2025-11-05).
- Alex: draft initial Private deployment runbook and minimal infra template for customer-managed runtime (due 2025-11-15).

Quick heuristics / notes to self
- If p95 latency requirement is strict, prefer Dedicated + pre-warm strategy rather than purely autoscaled Private runtime.
- Consider serving a smaller distilled model (e.g., 3–4B instruction-tuned) for short product blurb fallback to meet p95 when heavy burst.
- For cost: compute tokens per call = in_tokens + out_tokens; assume 1.4x token overhead for system prompts and chat metadata.

Meeting follow-up plan
- Send follow-up email with proposed bench plan and ask for trace logs + KMS contact.
- Set up 1:1 with Nexa infra lead to map networking constraints (aim next week).

Notes / rough TODOs
- Create eval harness repo: nexainfra/evals (skeleton) — include tokenized cost calculator, latency runner, and dataset loader.
- Add alert thresholds in Redwood Console: p95 > 350ms, fallback ratio > 1% during 5m window.
- Check with security: how to redaction PII before logs leave VPC.

Tags that might be useful for later search: Nexus? (actually Nexa), ecommerce, private-deploy, burst-capacity, se-oncall

End of scratchpad — keep iterative.
